nit: rename to `eraseLeftoverTemplateVars` or similar to be more precise in what this function does.

I’ve tested the patch and it resolves my issue. In my case, leaving the template variable as-is does not help with debugging, since it only confuses downstream users. Replacing it with an empty string makes the output clearer and avoids misinterpretation.

This patch was updated to not apply new template var config format, but simply find a left-over template var's boundary based on an implicit rule and replace it with an empty string. The commit message clarifies.

```suggestion
left-over
```
Done

Testing once with a real config would be nice. From what i have seen, the unit tests only cover the `templateCharReplace` stuff and not how and when it is called.

We can have a config with some real and some non-existent template vars and then logs and `busctl` output can show that some were correctly replaced and others could not be replaced.
Added real test result.

We may need to know the file and line number where the template var was found.

Otherwise it could be hard to track down if one has a lot of config.
Hi, is there a reference somewhere to extract file name and line num?

For filename, it would have to be passed through `templateCharReplace` and possibly other functions. The 

> Hi, is there a reference somewhere to extract file name and line num?

Other functions in EM simply dump the entire file but i don't like that, it does not help to debug. I did not find a reference where the filename is printed.

```
src/entity_manager/configuration.cpp
140:            std::cerr << "configuration file missing probe:\n " << *it << "\n";


src/entity_manager/perform_scan.cpp
372:        std::cerr << "configuration file dependency error, could not find "
535:            std::cerr << "configuration file missing probe:\n " << *it << "\n";
543:            std::cerr << "configuration file missing name:\n " << *it << "\n";
```

currently EM knows this information in `configuration.cpp`
https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/3911d80afb6956b17c4f4b9a76c7eb45bb76e3b9/src/entity_manager/configuration.cpp#L90

but its discarded after. May need to keep a map instead of vector for the configuration, to keep the filename around. Alternatively we could have a class to wrap both the filename and json.

For lohmann json, getting the line number is apparently not possible 
https://github.com/nlohmann/json/discussions/3949.
I apologize for suggesting this.
Ah, I see. Thanks for your info. Still, do you want me to proceed with the file name stuff?

It will be better to have a proper error message with filename, right?

But since the patch is fixing the existing bug (leftover template var is ignored without any message), i think it's fine to leave out the filename for now if that's too much work.
ACK. Thank you for your review.
